commentary: Broad market breadth has dropped to 47.4% with major equity indices like SPY and QQQ experiencing severe drawdowns (-9.7% and -13.6% over 1m) and breaching their 200-day moving averages. In contrast, fixed income sleeve assets (IEF, AGG, TLT) are delivering positive 1-month stability (+0.1% to +0.8%) with low annualized volatility (5.1% to 11.0%). The portfolio is being repositioned by harvesting capital from broken macro and cyclical equity theses (SPY, VEA, DBC, VNQ, JPM) where stated risks have materialised below 200-day averages. Capital is reallocated into non-cyclical, high-margin, low-beta momentum leaders across Consumer Staples and Health Care that remain firmly above their 200-day moving averages. What would change this view is an expansion of universe breadth back above 60% alongside bond yield spikes that break Treasury sleeve stability.
allocation_reason: Targeting a 0.33 bond sleeve weight places the portfolio 0.08 above the 0.25 minimum floor and 0.42 below the 0.75 maximum cap. This moderate allocation maintains necessary decorrelation and volatility ballast during market-wide equity contraction without over-allocating to long-end rate risk.
